questions.questionText: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Mars is called the Red Planet because iron oxide (rust) on its surface gives it a reddish appearance.

questions.questionText: How many continents are there on Earth?
questions.explanation: There are seven continents: Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Europe, North America, Oceania, and South America.

questions.questionText: What is the capital of France?
questions.explanation: Paris has been the capital of France for centuries and is home to the Eiffel Tower.

questions.questionText: Who wrote the play 'Romeo and Juliet'?
questions.explanation: William Shakespeare wrote 'Romeo and Juliet' in the late 16th century.

questions.questionText: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest of Earth's oceans.

questions.questionText: Which language has the most native speakers worldwide?
questions.explanation: Mandarin Chinese has the most native speakers of any language in the world.

questions.questionText: In which year did World War II end?
questions.explanation: World War II ended in 1945 following the surrender of the Axis powers.

questions.questionText: What is the currency used in Japan?
questions.explanation: The Japanese Yen is the official currency of Japan.

questions.questionText: Which instrument has 88 keys?
questions.explanation: A standard piano has 88 keys: 52 white and 36 black.

questions.questionText: What is the tallest mountain in the world above sea level?
questions.explanation: Mount Everest stands at about 8,849 meters, the highest point above sea level.

questions.questionText: What gas do plants absorb from the atmosphere for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen during photosynthesis.

questions.questionText: Which planet in our solar system is the fourth from the Sun?
questions.explanation: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun, right after Earth.

questions.questionText: What is the chemical symbol for water?
questions.explanation: Water is made of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom, giving it the formula H2O.

questions.questionText: What is the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria produce energy (ATP) and are known as the powerhouse of the cell.

questions.questionText: At what temperature does water boil at sea level (Celsius)?
questions.explanation: At sea level, water boils at 100 degrees Celsius (212°F).

questions.questionText: Which force keeps us grounded on Earth?
questions.explanation: Gravity is the force that attracts objects toward the center of the Earth.

questions.questionText: What is the hardest natural substance on Earth?
questions.explanation: Diamond is the hardest known natural material, made of pure carbon.

questions.questionText: How many bones are in the adult human body?
questions.explanation: The adult human body has 206 bones.

questions.questionText: What type of energy does a moving object have?
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is the energy an object possesses due to its motion.

questions.questionText: Which part of the plant conducts photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Leaves contain chlorophyll and are the main site of photosynthesis.
